$comment: A flow is a named journey. Each step names the surface it lands on and the
ATOMS the capture of that surface should show. The atom is the unit, not the
step and not the surface — a shared surface collects atoms from every flow
routed to it, and many of those cannot be answered by a still picture.
Measured: 21 'should see' lines from 19 different flows landed on one
navigation bar, including 'a spinner, then a fresh briefing, then a toast'.
Handing all 21 to a judge as the bar for that one image fails healthy
software loudly and confidently. Each atom is answered on its own, and
Copy this file, replace the contents, and feed it to both the capture pass
and the judge. Ids are stable: FLOW-002 and FLOW-002.03 are what a review
comment points at a year later.

flows.label: Publish a record
flows.$comment: critical:true means the campaign gate requires at least one case here at oracle rung outcome, metamorphic or visual. Presence-only proof of a critical flow is the failure that rule exists for.

steps.label: Open the record with two sections pending

atoms.text: the release bar names a count of pending changes
each pending section carries the reason it is pending
the sheet lists every pending change, none collapsed
a change can be reverted from the row it sits on
the confirm control states what will become public
the release bar reports nothing pending
the published-at instant is shown and is not a placeholder
the public page serves the new section
atoms.$comment: Expect not-observable in a still of the console. It is still worth declaring — the judge marks it not-observable with a reason, and the deterministic case at oracle rung `outcome` is what actually proves it.

flows.label: A refused write is reported as refused
flows.$comment: The honesty-guardrail flow. Force the server to refuse and assert the interface says so — see references/sweeps.md §H. Four live production defects of this class were invisible to every element-exists test, every screenshot and every visual judge.

steps.label: Attempt a change the server will refuse

atoms.text: the refusal sentence on screen is the server's own, not a local stand-in
the optimistic state has rolled back

$schema-notes.flow.id: stable, referenceable, and the anchor on the evidence page
$schema-notes.flow.critical: gates the oracle rung — see scripts/campaign.py
$schema-notes.flow.req: the requirements this flow serves; the gate traces every non-deferred requirement to at least one case
$schema-notes.step.surface: a key in surface-map.template.mjs — that file says where it lives; this one says what it should show
$schema-notes.step.state: the cell of the coverage model this step occupies
$schema-notes.step.atoms: one observable claim each. Write what a person would SEE, not what the code does.
